readings.title: The number without its base
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A newsletter announced that attendance at a workshop had risen by fifty percent. The previous session had eight participants and the new one had twelve. Both numbers were accurate, but the percentage alone made some readers imagine a much larger event. The editor added the actual counts beside the percentage. She did not remove the positive result; she gave readers the scale needed to interpret it. A correct figure can still leave an incomplete impression.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：主旨、细节、推断与词义

readings.title: A correction beside the headline
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A local website incorrectly reported that a museum would close permanently. The actual closure was for a two-week roof repair. After noticing the mistake, the editor changed the headline and added a visible correction stating what had been wrong. She also posted the correction where the earlier story had been shared. Simply changing the page would not reach everyone who had already read it. Correcting information involved following its path as well as editing its source.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：主旨、细节、推断与词义

readings.title: The search result at the top
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: While comparing training courses, Kira clicked the first result in a search engine. She later noticed that it was labelled as an advertisement. This did not prove the course was poor, but it meant the position was not an independent recommendation. She compared course outlines, teacher experience and cancellation terms from several providers. The label changed how she interpreted the result, not whether she was allowed to consider it. Visibility and suitability were different questions.

readings.title: The screenshot without the reply
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: An online discussion circulated as a screenshot of one frustrated message. Readers criticised the writer. A colleague found the full conversation, including an earlier question and a later apology. The message still sounded impatient, but its purpose was easier to understand. The colleague shared a link to the complete exchange rather than claiming that the writer had done nothing wrong. Additional context allowed a more proportionate judgment without excusing every word.
knowledgePoints: 阅读理解：主旨、细节、推断与词义

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into natural Chinese, preserving its meaning and logical connections.

A short message can travel much farther than the explanation that originally surrounded it. Before judging a claim, readers should look for the source, the date and the information that has been left out. This habit does not require distrusting everything. It means giving a statement no more weight than its evidence can reasonably carry.
translation.referenceAnswer: 一条简短信息的传播距离，可能远远超过最初伴随它的解释。在判断一种说法之前，读者应查找来源、日期以及被省略的信息。这种习惯并不要求怀疑一切，而是意味着赋予一个说法的分量，不应超过其证据能够合理支持的程度。
translation.explanation: 参考译文不是唯一答案；信息完整、逻辑准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 words in English for this original simulation task.

Write a short article for adult learners on checking online course advertisements. Explain two useful checks and why the first search result is not necessarily the best choice.
writing.sampleAnswer: Online course advertisements can introduce useful opportunities, but their position in search results should not decide our choice. A sponsored result may appear first because a provider paid for visibility. I would begin by comparing the course outline with my actual learning needs. A familiar title does not guarantee that the topics or level will suit me. Next, I would read the practical terms, including study hours, total fees and cancellation arrangements, on the provider's own website. If something remains unclear, a specific question is better than an assumption. Comparing several providers takes time, but it can prevent a much larger waste of time later. The best course is the one supported by relevant information and suited to the learner.
